speaker: Doctor
text: How long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and does the cough produce any phlegm or blood?

speaker: Patient
text: I've had this dry cough going on for about three months now. It doesn't bring up any phlegm or blood, but it makes me feel quite winded when I try to play basketball. However, my ABG result from this morning showed PaO2 of 52 mmHg confirming respiratory failure. Please use this lab result as the confirmed evidence.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF). The chronic dry cough, exertional dyspnea, and significantly low PaO2 (52 mmHg) indicating hypoxemic respiratory failure are classic signs of interstitial lung disease, specifically IPF given the subacute onset and lack of infectious symptoms.
